summary: Iteration 7: validated the new Studio multi-brand outfit grid (OutfitGrid.jsx + /api/outfit/generate-from-uploads + /api/wardrobe/garments/from-screenshot). 13/13 backend pytests pass. Frontend E2E on /studio: existing upload-person, upload-garment, generate-tryon-btn, privacy-box-top, privacy-box-bottom are unchanged; new outfit-grid-section renders with title 'COMPONI IL TUO OUTFIT MULTI-BRAND - FINO A 4 CAPI' and the 4 slots in a 2x2 grid (top/bottom/jacket/shoes). File upload via grid-slot-<k>-input shows preview; grid-slot-<k>-clear removes it; .txt upload is rejected with Italian toast 'Formato non supportato: usa jpg, png o webp'. grid-generate-btn is disabled with 0 garments and enabled with >=1 valid upload. Real AI generation was NOT re-run (main agent already executed one successful 13s run).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 1744 lines — still growing (iteration 6 flagged 1646). Strongly recommend splitting outfit, wardrobe and files into dedicated routers before adding more features.
server.py outfit_generate_from_uploads: validates 1-4 slots, unknown slot keys, foreign path ownership and 402 quota before any AI call. _compose_outfit is shared with outfit_generate — DRY, good.
server.py wardrobe_save_from_screenshot: slot whitelist, URL regex, ownership all enforced before meta fetch; falls back to generic name/brand when _fetch_page/_extract_product_meta fail (per spec).

OutfitGrid.jsx: slots whitelist constant mirrors backend _GRID_SLOTS. Accept list uses MIME types only — some drag&drop sources may provide empty type for jpg (would trip the ACCEPT check); file input also uses extension list which is correct. If users report 'Formato non supportato' on valid jpg via DnD, allow empty type when extension is .jpg/.png/.webp.
OutfitGrid.jsx: no cleanup of URL.createObjectURL(preview) when slot is replaced/cleared — minor memory leak over long sessions.
OutfitGrid.jsx generate(): correctly checks !personPath with toast asking to upload foto; does not open paywall unless status.is_blocked.
SaveLinkRow uses item.path (uploaded screenshot) as the garment image_path — the saved wardrobe entry reuses the same storage object, so no duplicate upload. Good.
GridItem Pydantic model lacks field validation (max length / path format). Backend relies on _path_owner regex-ish check; acceptable but a Field(regex=...) would be stricter.
